analysis.title: Americas Technology: Semiconductors: 3Q Preview: Expect stocks to work on better numbers following sector-wide pullback
key_insights: GS sees upside to estimates across most semiconductor sub-sectors heading into 3Q earnings, with the most estimate upside in SemiCap, compute and storage. The setup is described as more constructive than 2Q, when GS was tactically cautious.
The sector pulled back over the past two months on significant de-risking, with SOX down 11% versus SPX up 4%. GS says risk/reward is now more favorable going into results.
SemiCap: GS expects significant positive estimate revisions because of pull-ins to wafer fab equipment (WFE) spending and long-term visibility into 2028.
Compute: an upward bias to hyperscaler CapEx supports upside for server CPUs (rising agentic AI attach) and key ASIC programs. AMD, INTC and QCOM all carry server or datacenter CPU narratives.

Analog: GS is favorable on upside to estimates and prefers names with the most industrial, aero/defense and datacenter exposure. It says the Street under-models the analog recovery and calls MCHP among its favorite names.
Memory/storage: GS sees fundamental upside but prefers HDDs and NAND because there are no near-term supply additions. STX is preferred over WDC on faster HAMR progress.

Tactical ideas: upside for AMAT, STX and MCHP, downside for QCOM, KLAC and WDC. QCOM is seen as ahead of itself on agentic AI expectations. KLAC and WDC are expected to lag peers (KLAC on DRAM-skewed WFE, WDC versus STX on HAMR).

AMD (Buy): PT raised to $700 from $640 on a 32X P/E applied to normalized EPS of $22 (up from $20). 2026/27/28 EPS moves to $8.05/$17.10/$25.20 from $8.05/$16.30/$23.70. 2027 EPS is 7% above Street. Focus is Helios contribution in 4Q, server CPU demand and margins.

ARM (Sell, PT $160 on 50X normalized EPS of $3.20): GS expects an in-line quarter with EPS guidance above consensus. Persistent smartphone weakness is a near-term royalty risk. Supply for the AGI CPU is the key swing, with $2bn of FY27-28 demand cited and an incremental $1bn constrained by supply.
ARM debate: GS checks suggest Meta's Muse agentic product runs predominantly on x86, so investors will watch ARM versus x86 share trends.

CDNS (Buy, PT $470): GS expects CY26 revenue growth guidance raised to ~21% from ~18%, driven by core EDA and hardware. The stock rallied ~15% over two weeks, so expectations have risen. 2027 EPS is ~4% above Street.

INTC (Neutral, PT $150): GS is well above Street on 2027 (EPS $2.75 vs $2.06) and 2028 (EPS $4.70 vs $3.19) on server CPU strength, foundry and gross margin. Much of the near-term upside is seen as priced in.

QCOM (Neutral, PT $180 unchanged): GS expects an in-line FY4Q with modest upside to 1Q guidance and models $600mn of datacenter revenue in 1Q. EPS estimates are cut ~3% on component cost inflation. Investor expectations are seen as too high in the short term.

MCHP (Buy, PT $115): GS expects ~1% revenue upside and low-single-digit QoQ guidance, with gross margin recovering to ~66% exiting CY26. FY27 EPS is ~3% above Street. Datacenter is ~17% of revenue with a $1bn CY26 revenue target.
NXPI (Buy, PT $325): GS expects an in-line quarter with ~1% revenue and 40bps margin upside. Focus is automotive (China and Europe), datacenter doubling target and price increases flowing to margins.

ON (Neutral, PT $95): GS expects a solid quarter with focus on datacenter power (800V), automotive (~50% of revenue) and the proposed Synaptics acquisition, expected to close mid-2027. Neutral because SiC/CIS headwinds may offset the industrial/auto recovery.
SITM (Buy, PT $900): GS expects a beat-and-raise with ~5% revenue upside and QoQ guide of ~4.5%, driven by datacenter and aerospace. The Renesas acquisition closed ahead of schedule.

TXN (relative Sell, PT $225): GS expects ~3% revenue upside and 4Q guidance ~2% above Street. Sell reflects expected gross margin lag versus peers on elevated inventory and D&A. Focus is 300mm fab utilization and the $8/share 2026 FCF target.

AMAT (Buy, conviction-list, PT $670): ahead of SEMICON West on Oct. 13, GS expects management to speak to a WFE market growing to $300bn over time and higher long-term margin targets. The stock rallied ~12% in the past week. CY26 non-GAAP EPS is 3% above Street.

LRCX (Buy, PT $380): the stock is down ~20% over three months, which GS says improves risk/reward. GS expects upside on GAA and backside power deposition and etch exposure, DRAM share gains and NAND upgrades. CY4Q26 EPS is ~7% above Street and the company has a ~55% gross margin target.

KLAC (Neutral, PT $210): management guided CY26 and CY27 growth to the mid-20% range, which GS says lags more bullish WFE forecasts. GS expects ~5% revenue upside but results lagging peers because WFE is skewed to DRAM. Memory costs remain a gross margin headwind into CY27.

Other SemiCap: AMKR (Neutral, PT $65) has ~2% revenue upside on 2.5D/HDFO demand. CAMT (Neutral, PT $160) is in line for the quarter but CY27 EPS is ~12% below Street. ENTG (Sell, PT $120) has revenue upside and in-line CY27 EPS. GFS (Neutral, PT $70) is well above Street on CY26 EPS with silicon photonics/CPO in focus. MKSI (Sell, PT $270) is in line with CY27 EPS 3% below Street. ONTO (Buy, PT $400) has ~2% revenue upside and CY27 EPS ~6% above Street. Q (Buy, PT $175) has 3%-4% revenue upside and CY27 EPS ~11% above Street. TER (Buy, PT $465) has ~3% revenue upside with AI test intensity and CPO in focus.

SNDK (Buy, PT $2,200): GS expects ~5% upside to Street and ~6% to the guidance midpoint, with CY26 non-GAAP EPS ~6% above Street. Focus is long-term agreement (LTA) coverage, NAND supply and the HBF opportunity.

STX (Buy, PT $960): GS expects ~2% revenue upside and FQ2 guidance ~3% above Street on tight HDD supply and HAMR mix. Out-year EPS (2027 to 2029) is below Street. Capital returns and HAMR progress are the focus.

WDC (Neutral, PT $615): GS expects ~1% revenue upside and guidance ~1% above Street. Prefers STX because of the faster HAMR ramp. Last quarter's exabyte growth came in below long-term targets, and 2027/2028 EPS sits well below Street.

trade_ideas.description: Tactical long AMAT into SEMICON West (Oct. 13) and earnings
trade_ideas.rationale: GS expects raised margin targets, a WFE outlook toward $300bn and a strong report driven by DRAM and advanced logic.
trade_ideas.risk: Incremental export restrictions and local China-based supplier share gains.

trade_ideas.rationale: Tight HDD supply, positive pricing and HAMR progress support ~2% revenue upside and guidance ~3% above Street.
trade_ideas.risk: Difficulties qualifying HAMR at major hyperscalers and lack of supply-side prudence.

trade_ideas.rationale: Broad industrial demand plus aerospace/defense and datacenter upside, with the Street under-modeling the analog recovery.
trade_ideas.risk: Timing of the analog and MCU recovery, and balance sheet inventory delaying margin expansion.

trade_ideas.description: Tactical downside view on QCOM into earnings
trade_ideas.rationale: Stock may be ahead of itself given very strong investor expectations tied to agentic AI and CPU vendors.
trade_ideas.risk: Stronger-than-expected datacenter CPU traction and stabilizing smartphone share.

trade_ideas.description: Tactical downside view on KLAC into earnings
trade_ideas.rationale: Results expected to lag peers as WFE spending is skewed toward DRAM, despite upside to the quarter and guidance.
trade_ideas.risk: Sharp increase in Foundry/Logic spending or a sharp rebound in Memory WFE spending.

trade_ideas.description: Tactical downside view on WDC versus STX
trade_ideas.rationale: WDC is expected to underperform STX because the HAMR ramp drives STX's stronger near-term exabyte growth and gross margin expansion.
trade_ideas.risk: Pull-in of WDC's HAMR roadmap or new consumer/enterprise storage applications.

risk_factors: Slower than expected adoption of agentic AI and slower AMD GPU deployment tied to the Meta deal.
Share erosion of x86 in enterprise AI (AMD) and ARM versus x86 share trends in agentic AI.
Persistent smartphone weakness hitting ARM royalties, QCOM handsets and GFS smart mobile.
Export restrictions, tariffs and local China supplier share gains affecting SemiCap names.
Timing of the analog and automotive recovery, and inventory delaying margin expansion.
Slower AI datacenter spending or hyperscaler CapEx.
NAND supply additions, particularly in China (YMTC), and HDD industry overshipping or lack of supply discipline.
Component cost inflation and memory costs pressuring margins (QCOM, KLAC).
PFAS litigation liabilities and the CFO transition at Qnity.
vol_and_positioning: The sector de-risked sharply over the past two months, with SOX down 11% versus SPX up 4%, which GS says leaves a more constructive trading setup into earnings.

Investor positioning by name: bullish on SITM, LRCX, ONTO, MKSI and AMKR-like balanced, neutral on MCHP and CAMT, cautious on ON after the Synaptics deal pullback, slightly negatively biased on KLAC, and positively positioned on TXN and STX.
AMAT rallied ~12% in the past week and CDNS ~15% over two weeks, so GS says expectations are elevated for both.

LRCX is down ~20% over three months, MKSI down ~7% since its last report, and SITM underperformed SOXX in the quarter (~-7.5% vs ~-5.4% for SOXX and ~-9.5% for GS analog coverage). TXN is ~-6% vs ~-10% for analog peers.
GS says QCOM expectations are very strong on agentic AI, creating tactical downside risk.
geopolitical: Export restrictions are listed as a downside risk for AMAT, CDNS and KLAC, and incremental US export restrictions for KLAC.
Local China-based supplier share gains are named as a downside risk for AMAT.
Tariffs and export restrictions are named as a risk for Qnity.
GS notes TSMC exits the GaN market in 2027, which GFS could capture share from.
cross_bank_references: Cadence expected to give positive commentary on momentum in recurring revenue growth, in line with peer Synopsys' positive commentary at its Investor Day.

tension_points.bull_case: AI infrastructure spending is resilient, AGI CPU demand is cited at $2 bn for FY27-28 and server CPU and datacenter strength support royalties.
tension_points.bear_case: Persistent smartphone weakness offsets CPU and datacenter strength, supply limits an incremental $1 bn of AGI CPU demand, and GS checks suggest Meta's Muse agent runs mostly on x86.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Securing incremental AGI CPU supply or improved margin visibility on that business would strengthen the bull side, while no smartphone recovery visibility keeps royalties pressured.

tension_points.bull_case: Outsized growth in advanced packaging and N2/GAA migrations drives more process control, and GS expects ~5% revenue upside.
tension_points.bear_case: Management guided CY26 and CY27 growth to the mid-20% range despite more bullish WFE forecasts, and WFE spending is skewed to DRAM where KLAC has less exposure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sharp increase in Foundry/Logic spending, or a rebound in process control intensity as a share of WFE, would invalidate the lag thesis.

tension_points.bull_case: STX has advanced HAMR progress and a prudent supply strategy that should drive incremental HDD share gains.
tension_points.bear_case: WDC is constructive on HDD pricing, but HAMR transition costs may pressure margins and last quarter's exabyte growth was below long-term targets.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A pull-in of WDC's HAMR roadmap, or STX HAMR qualification difficulties at major hyperscalers, would change the relative call.

tension_points.bull_case: Initial datacenter shipments in 1Q and agentic AI benefit to CPU vendors support strong FY27 traction.
tension_points.bear_case: Investor expectations are too high in the short term and handset recovery remains unclear, with margins pressured by component cost inflation.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Stronger-than-expected traction for datacenter CPUs or stabilizing smartphone share would invalidate the tactical caution.
